italian-game.name: Scholar's Mate Danger
italian-game.description: The queen and bishop both aim at f7. Black must answer that shared threat before developing the king knight.

trap_line.explanation: This develops a piece but leaves f7 attacked twice.
The queen takes on f7 with the bishop protecting it. The king has no safe reply.

italian-game.success_message: The mate works only because Black ignored the two attackers on f7.
italian-game.danger: White's queen and bishop are both attacking f7.
italian-game.how_to_avoid: Defend f7 and block the queen-bishop attack before starting another plan.

defense_line.explanation: The queen guards f7. Now Qxf7 is no longer mate and Black can develop safely.

italian-game.name: Fried Liver Attack
italian-game.description: White attacks f7 with the bishop and knight. Black must strike the center, then move the c6 knight instead of recapturing on d5.
italian-game.danger: After Ng5, the bishop on c4 and knight on g5 both attack f7. The natural Nxd5 recapture allows Nxf7 and pulls the king into danger.
italian-game.how_to_avoid: Play ...d5, and after exd5 move the c6 knight to a5. Do not recapture on d5 while f7 is attacked twice.

defense_line.explanation: Black attacks the bishop and opens a route for the c6 knight to leave safely.
White captures on d5 and renews the pressure on f7.
The knight leaves c6 without stepping onto d5. Black attacks the bishop and avoids the king chase.

trap_line.explanation: Black tries to block, but it's too late...
White captures the pawn.
Black recaptures, but the knight is vulnerable.
White gives up the knight on f7 to pull Black's king away from safety.
Black must capture.
Check! Double attack on king and knight on d5.
The king is forced forward into danger.
White develops the other knight toward d5 while Black's king remains exposed. The attack is dangerous, but it is not an automatic material win.

italian-game.success_message: The sacrifice has pulled Black's king to e6. White has attacking chances, not a guaranteed material win.

italian-game.name: Legal's Mate
italian-game.danger: White's knight on e5 appears to leave the queen on d1 unprotected, but taking the queen allows a forced mate.
italian-game.how_to_avoid: Do not take the queen. Capture the knight on e5 and remove the mating attack first.

defense_line.explanation: The d6 pawn captures the knight. Black removes an attacker instead of opening the path to Bxf7+.

italian-game.description: A beautiful queen sacrifice leading to checkmate.

trap_line.explanation: Sacrifice! Offering the queen to set up checkmate.
Black takes the queen, falling into the trap!
Check! The king must move.
Forced - the only legal move.
Checkmate! The Legal's Mate - a queen sacrifice for mate.

italian-game.success_message: Legal's Mate! A beautiful queen sacrifice leading to checkmate.

italian-game.name: Blackburne Shilling Gambit
italian-game.danger: The pawn on e5 is bait. If White's knight takes it, Black's queen can attack g2 and start a mating attack.
italian-game.how_to_avoid: Take Black's knight on d4 instead of the pawn on e5.

defense_line.explanation: White removes the advanced knight. The e5 pawn can wait, and Black's queen never gets the attack on g2.

italian-game.description: A cunning trap where Black sacrifices a pawn to deliver checkmate!

trap_line.explanation: White takes the pawn - a natural but losing move!
Threatening Qxg2 and the knight on e5.
White tries to complicate with a fork...
Black ignores the threat and attacks f1!
White defends.
Check! Picks up the e4 pawn while forcing an answer.
Blocking with the bishop.
Checkmate! The knight delivers the final blow.

italian-game.success_message: Blackburne Shilling Gambit Mate! A devastating trap for Black.

italian-game.name: Scholar's Mate Defense Trap
italian-game.danger: Black's knight check on c2 forks the king and rook. Moving the king lets the knight take the rook on a1.
italian-game.how_to_avoid: Capture the checking knight with the queen instead of moving the king.

defense_line.explanation: The queen takes the checking knight. White keeps the rook on a1 and ends Black's fork.

italian-game.description: Punish White's premature queen attack and win material!

trap_line.explanation: The knight jumps to a powerful, safe square!
White tries to threaten f7.
Fork! The knight attacks king and rook.
The king moves.
Black wins the exchange - rook for knight!

italian-game.success_message: Scholar's Mate refuted! You won material by exploiting White's greedy play.

italian-game.name: Traxler Counterattack
italian-game.learning_goal: When White attacks f7 with Ng5, learn how ...Bc5 creates threats against White's king instead of defending passively.
italian-game.description: Black's daring counter-trap against the Fried Liver setup — if white takes on f7, black launches a king-hunt.

trap_line.explanation: White grabs f7, and Black chooses a counterattack instead of defending quietly.
Black's counter-sacrifice! Bishop gives check.
White chooses to take the bishop. Ke2 and Kf1 are also legal, so this is one sharp branch rather than a forced reply.
The knight checks the king, so White must answer while Black's queen prepares to join.
King walks forward — the hunt is on.
The queen joins the attack with more checks available. White still has defensive choices, so Black must calculate rather than assume mate.

italian-game.success_message: The Traxler turns the attack on f7 into a sharp king-hunt, but it does not force one reply or promise an automatic win.

italian-game.name: Lolli Variation
italian-game.learning_goal: Use d4 and castling to add the rook to the attack after Black recaptures on d5.
italian-game.description: In the Two Knights, White plays d4 before sacrificing on f7 so castling can bring the rook toward the attack.

trap_line.explanation: White challenges the knight on d5 and opens the c1 bishop.
Black accepts another pawn and opens the e-file.
White brings the rook to the open e-file before starting the f7 sacrifice.
Black develops and prepares to move the king to safety.
Only now does White take on f7, with the rook ready to use the opened e-file.

italian-game.success_message: The Lolli idea is move order: open the center and castle before sacrificing on f7.

sicilian-defense.name: Siberian Trap
sicilian-defense.danger: After Black checks on c3, blocking with Bd2 leaves White's queen exposed to the exchange on d2.
sicilian-defense.how_to_avoid: Capture the checking bishop with the b-pawn. Do not place the bishop on d2 in front of the queen.

defense_line.explanation: The b-pawn removes the checking bishop. White's queen stays safe on d1.

sicilian-defense.description: A deadly trap where Black wins White's queen with a series of checks!

trap_line.explanation: White attacks the knight - a common but losing move!
Black threatens Bxc3+ winning the queen.
White captures, but falls into the trap...
Check! The bishop takes the knight with check.
White blocks the check.
Take the bishop with another check!
White must take with the queen.
The Siberian Trap! Black wins White's queen.

sicilian-defense.success_message: The Siberian Trap! Black wins White's queen for just a knight.

sicilian-defense.name: Magnus Smith Attack Plan
sicilian-defense.learning_goal: Use e5-e6 to open the diagonal toward f7 after Black's queenside pawns are damaged.
sicilian-defense.description: A sharp Dragon idea: exchange on c6, then use e5-e6 to open lines toward Black's king.

trap_line.explanation: White exchanges knights.
Black recaptures with the pawn.
A powerful pawn thrust!
The knight retreats.
The pawn advances to open lines around Black's king.
Black chooses to capture the advanced pawn.
White recaptures and restores material equality. The bishop becomes active while Black's queenside pawns remain split.

sicilian-defense.success_message: The e-pawn clears lines toward f7 while Black's queenside pawns remain split.

sicilian-defense.name: Wing Gambit
sicilian-defense.learning_goal: Trade a flank pawn for faster development and a larger pawn center without pretending the pawn sacrifice wins by force.
sicilian-defense.description: White sacrifices a flank pawn early to seize the centre against the Sicilian.

trap_line.explanation: Black accepts the pawn — most natural.
White offers another pawn to clear the b-file and build the centre.
If Black takes, White's d4 and rapid development give a big attack.
Knight develops while attacking, eyeing b5 and c4.
Black tries to hold — but White has open lines and lead in development.

sicilian-defense.success_message: Wing Gambit — pawn for a big centre and quick development against the Sicilian.

queens-gambit.name: Elephant Trap
queens-gambit.danger: The pawn on d5 looks free, but taking it lets Black trade on d5 and then check with Bb4+, winning White's queen-side pieces.
queens-gambit.how_to_avoid: Finish development with e3 instead of taking the d5 pawn a second time.

defense_line.explanation: White supports the center and opens the f1 bishop. The knight does not step onto the bait square d5.

queens-gambit.description: Black wins a piece with a beautiful intermezzo check!

trap_line.explanation: Black recaptures the pawn.
White thinks they win the queen! But...
Intermezzo! Check with the bishop.
White blocks with the queen.
Take the queen with check!
White must recapture.
Now Black takes back the bishop. You're up a full piece!

queens-gambit.success_message: The Elephant Trap! The intermezzo check wins a piece.

queens-gambit.name: Lasker Trap
queens-gambit.description: A sharp queen trap in the Albin Counter-Gambit!
queens-gambit.danger: After the black pawn reaches e3, taking the bishop on b4 lets that pawn run to g1 with check and opens Black's bishop and queen toward d1.
queens-gambit.how_to_avoid: Do not take the bishop on b4. Capture the pawn on e3 before it reaches f2.

defense_line.explanation: The f-pawn removes the advanced pawn before it can check on f2 or promote on g1.

trap_line.explanation: White takes the bishop, but...
The pawn advances with check!
The king steps up.
Underpromotion to knight with check! A rare move.
White takes the knight.
Check! And the queen falls next move.
White moves back, but the queen on d1 remains exposed along the open file.
Black's queen takes White's queen on d1 with check.

queens-gambit.success_message: The Lasker Trap with underpromotion! A sharp queen trap.

queens-gambit.name: Rubinstein Trap
queens-gambit.danger: The pin on Black's knight can make the d5 and h7 pawns look easier to win than they are. Black must finish development before starting a pawn chase.
queens-gambit.how_to_avoid: Develop the f8 bishop and prepare to castle before spending a move on a6.

defense_line.explanation: Black breaks the pin, prepares to castle, and keeps the center defended.

queens-gambit.description: A deep QGD trap where black's careless a6 allows a tactical sequence that wins a pawn through a pin against h7.

trap_line.explanation: Trades center pawns — opens the e-file for white.
Black recaptures.
Trades the pinned knight.
Black recaptures with the knight.
Nxd5! Black can't take back — Qxh7 would be mate.

queens-gambit.success_message: The Rubinstein Trap — a careless a6 lets white win a pawn via the h7 pin.

queens-gambit.name: Cambridge Springs Trap
queens-gambit.danger: After ...Qa5, Black pressures c3 and can play ...Ne4. The careless Bd3 and Qc2 setup lets Black remove the g5 bishop and then the f3 knight.
queens-gambit.how_to_avoid: Meet ...Qa5 with Nd2, cxd5, or Bxf6. Each move addresses Black's pressure before routine development.

defense_line.explanation: Nd2 unpins the c3 knight and meets Black's ...Ne4 pressure before developing the bishop.

queens-gambit.description: In the Cambridge Springs, ...Qa5 and ...Ne4 combine pressure on c3 with an attack on the bishop on g5. White must answer that coordination before playing routine moves.

trap_line.explanation: Black centralizes while attacking the bishop on g5 and increases the pressure around c3.
White develops the queen but leaves both the g5 bishop and f3 knight in the tactical sequence.
Black's knight removes the bishop on g5.
White's f3 knight recaptures on g5.
Black moves the d5 pawn, opening the fifth rank from the queen on a5 to the knight on g5.
White recaptures the pawn but does not close the queen's line.
The queen takes the knight on g5. Black has won a bishop through the ...Ne4 and fifth-rank combination.

queens-gambit.success_message: Cambridge Springs tactic — ...Ne4 removes the g5 bishop, then ...dxc4 opens the queen's path to the recapturing knight.

queens-gambit.name: Marshall Defense Center Lesson
queens-gambit.learning_goal: Challenge 2...Nf6 immediately, gain central space, and use development rather than hunting for a tactical trick.
queens-gambit.description: The Queen's Gambit Marshall Defense starts with 2...Nf6. White's practical lesson is to exchange on d5, gain space with e4, and develop while Black's knight has to move again.

trap_line.explanation: White challenges the unsupported d5 pawn immediately.
Black recaptures with the knight, which now becomes a target for a central pawn.
White gains central space and makes the knight move again.
Black preserves the knight but has spent another move.
White develops, supports the center, and prepares to castle.

queens-gambit.danger: If White treats 2...Nf6 like a normal Queen's Gambit position, Black may transpose without paying for the early knight move.
queens-gambit.how_to_avoid: Challenge the center with cxd5, then choose a sound space gain or development plan. There is no need to invent a forced tactical win.

defense_line.explanation: White asks the central question immediately instead of allowing an effortless transposition.

queens-gambit.success_message: Marshall Defense lesson — challenge d5, gain central space, and develop while the knight moves again.

queens-gambit.name: QGA Greedy ...b5 Trap (Qf3)
queens-gambit.danger: After a4, ...c6 places the c-pawn on the a8-h1 diagonal. If that pawn recaptures on b5, Qf3 attacks the rook on a8 through the opened diagonal.
queens-gambit.how_to_avoid: Answer a4 with ...a6 instead of ...c6. The a-pawn supports b5 without opening a diagonal to the rook.

defense_line.explanation: The a-pawn supports b5 while the c-pawn stays on c7 and keeps the diagonal to a8 closed.

queens-gambit.description: When Black tries to hold the c4 gambit pawn with ...b5, the central diagonal becomes vulnerable. White invites with a4; if Black defends with ...c6 instead of ...a6, the axb5 cxb5 sequence opens the a8-h1 diagonal and Qf3 wins the rook on a8. The reason White plays the Queen's Gambit: Black usually shouldn't try to hold the pawn — and when they do, tactics like this punish it.

trap_line.explanation: The greedy defense. Black tries to hold b5 with the c-pawn, but this opens the a8-h1 diagonal. ...a6 was the safer try.
White captures, threatening b5 again — Black has no choice but to recapture.
Forced recapture. Now the a8-h1 diagonal is wide open and the rook on a8 has no defender.
Wins the rook on a8 along the open diagonal. The c4 gambit pawn was never worth the structural damage.
Black develops, but no piece can close the a8-h1 diagonal in time.
White's queen reaches a8 and captures the rook.

queens-gambit.success_message: QGA Greedy ...b5 Trap. axb5 cxb5 opens the a8-h1 diagonal; Qf3 wins the rook on a8.

london-system.name: Englund Gambit Trap
london-system.danger: Black's queen has grabbed b2, but retreating to b4 lets White's bishop trap it.
london-system.how_to_avoid: Use Bb4 to pin White's c3 bishop toward the king on e1 and give the queen an escape route.

defense_line.explanation: The bishop pins White's bishop on c3 along the diagonal toward the king on e1 and stops Bxb4.

london-system.description: Refute the dubious Englund Gambit and trap Black's queen!

trap_line.explanation: Block the check with the bishop.
Black takes the pawn greedily, but...
The queen is trapped! No safe squares.
Black tries to escape, but...
Take the queen! She has nowhere to run.

london-system.success_message: The Englund Gambit refuted! Black's greed costs them the queen.

caro-kann.name: Caro-Kann Smothered Mate
caro-kann.danger: Both black knights can move to f6, but the g8 knight blocks the king's last escape squares and allows Nd6 mate.
caro-kann.how_to_avoid: Use the knight from d7 to reach f6 and keep the g8 knight from sealing in the king.

defense_line.explanation: The d7 knight reaches f6. The g8 knight stays available, so White no longer has the same smothered mate.

caro-kann.description: A rare smothered mate in the Caro-Kann!

trap_line.explanation: Smothered Mate! The knight delivers checkmate.

caro-kann.success_message: Smothered Mate! Black's pieces block all escape squares.

caro-kann.name: Caro-Kann Classical Pin
caro-kann.learning_goal: Use h5 and Bd3 to question Black's active bishop, then recapture without damaging your pawn structure.
caro-kann.description: White chases Black's bishop to h7 with h5, then trades it off with Bd3. Black loses the bishop pair and White gets a strong position. Black should consider Bg4 instead of Bg6 to avoid the h4-h5 chase.

trap_line.explanation: White gains space and asks the g6 bishop where it will go.
Black keeps the bishop but places it on the edge of the board.
White offers a bishop trade before Black can bring the h7 bishop back into play.
Black exchanges bishops instead of leaving the h7 bishop shut out.
The queen recaptures, develops, and keeps White's pawns connected.

caro-kann.success_message: The h5-Bd3 plan trades Black's active bishop while White keeps a healthy pawn structure.

kings-indian-defense.name: King's Indian Bayonet Attack Plan
kings-indian-defense.learning_goal: In the Bayonet Attack, support the queenside space gain while watching for the central e6 jump.
kings-indian-defense.description: A Bayonet Attack model line where White gains queenside space, then uses e6 as a central entry square.

trap_line.explanation: Preventing Nf4.
Black pushes the f-pawn to create threats against White's king.
The knight eyes e6.
Black defends.
A solid, careful move.
Black tries to break.
Developing with purpose.
Kicking the knight.
The knight invades!
Black chooses to remove the knight. Other replies are legal, so this lesson follows the capture branch.
White creates an advanced passed pawn on e6. It is not protected yet, so White's next job is to support it.

kings-indian-defense.success_message: The Bayonet plan joins queenside space with a central knight jump and an advanced passed pawn that still needs support.

scandinavian-defense.name: Main-Line Scandinavian Bishop-Pin Plan
scandinavian-defense.learning_goal: After the queen recaptures on d5, use ...Bg4 to pin the f3 knight and develop while White spends pawn moves chasing the bishop.
scandinavian-defense.description: This is a main-line Scandinavian plan after 2...Qxd5, not the Portuguese Gambit. Black uses ...Qa5, ...Nf6, and ...Bg4 for active development.

trap_line.explanation: White kicks the bishop.
The bishop retreats but maintains the pin.
White attacks aggressively, but...
The bishop retreats again.
White centralizes.
Solid development.
Attacking the queen.
The queen retreats.
White develops. Black has active pieces and can create threats of their own.

scandinavian-defense.success_message: The Scandinavian bishop-pin plan gives Black active pieces while White spends time chasing the bishop.

scandinavian-defense.name: Scandinavian Queen Danger
scandinavian-defense.learning_goal: Develop with Bd2, then move the c3-knight so the bishop's diagonal reaches Black's queen on a5.
scandinavian-defense.description: A Scandinavian model plan: Bd2 points toward a5, and Nd5 clears c3 so the bishop—not the knight—attacks Black's queen. The knight also adds pressure to c7 and f6.

trap_line.explanation: White develops the bishop and prepares to move a rook toward the open files.
Black gives the queen a retreat square and supports d5.
Moving the knight clears c3, so the bishop on d2 now attacks the queen on a5 along d2-c3-b4-a5. The knight itself attacks c7 and f6.

scandinavian-defense.success_message: White uses a discovered bishop attack to make Black move the queen while the knight reaches an active square.

ruy-lopez.name: Noah's Ark Trap
ruy-lopez.danger: Taking the pawn on d4 lets Black chase the queen with ...c5 and ...Be6, then play ...c4 so the bishop on b3 has no safe retreat.
ruy-lopez.how_to_avoid: Do not take the d4 pawn with the queen. Castle and keep c3 available as a retreat square for the bishop.

defense_line.explanation: White leaves the d4 pawn alone, secures the king, and keeps c3 open for the b3 bishop.

ruy-lopez.description: A classic trap that wins White's light-squared bishop!

trap_line.explanation: White takes the pawn.
Attack the queen!
The queen retreats.
Attack the queen again!
White checks.
Block and attack the queen.
The queen moves.
The Noah's Ark Trap! The bishop is trapped.
The bishop gives itself up for the c4 pawn because every retreat square is covered.
Black's b-pawn captures the bishop and completes the material win.

ruy-lopez.success_message: Noah's Ark Trap! White's bishop has no escape.

ruy-lopez.name: Mortimer Trap
ruy-lopez.danger: The e5 pawn looks loose after Black's knight moves to e7, but Nxe5 lets Black chase the knight and open a mating attack.
ruy-lopez.how_to_avoid: Build the center with d4 or castle instead of grabbing e5.

defense_line.explanation: White strengthens the center and opens lines without sending the knight onto the bait square e5.

ruy-lopez.description: A beautiful smothered mate in the Ruy Lopez!

trap_line.explanation: White takes the pawn, but...
Attacking the bishop.
The knight moves.
Black takes the bishop.
Smothered Mate! Beautiful.

ruy-lopez.success_message: The Mortimer Trap! Smothered mate in the Ruy Lopez.

ruy-lopez.name: Tarrasch Trap (Open Lopez)
ruy-lopez.danger: After White plays Nd4, ...Qd7 protects the bishop but leaves Black unable to recapture on e6 without losing the knight on e4.
ruy-lopez.how_to_avoid: Remove the knight on d4 with ...Nxd4 instead of tying the queen to e6.

defense_line.explanation: Black removes the d4 knight before it can exchange on e6 and expose the knight on e4.

ruy-lopez.description: In the Open Ruy Lopez, ...Qd7 tries to protect e6 but allows White to exchange there and then capture the knight on e4.

trap_line.explanation: Black protects the bishop on e6, but the queen will be tied to any recapture there.
White's knight captures the bishop and forces Black's queen to recapture.
The queen restores the piece count but no longer protects the knight on e4.
White's rook captures the loose knight on e4 and wins a piece.

ruy-lopez.success_message: The exchange on e6 pulls Black's queen away from e4, so White's rook can take the knight.

ruy-lopez.name: Fishing Pole Trap
ruy-lopez.danger: After ...Ng4, h3 and hxg4 open the h-file for Black's rook and queen while White's own pawns take away the king's escape squares.
ruy-lopez.how_to_avoid: Do not chase the knight with h3. Play d4 and challenge the center before Black can open the h-file.

defense_line.explanation: White attacks the center and leaves the h-pawn on h2, so Black cannot open the h-file with ...h5.

ruy-lopez.description: The h-pawn sacrifice rips open the h-file. After hxg4 hxg4+, the king is exposed and mate threats follow on the h-file. After Ng4, do NOT play h3. Play d4 instead.

trap_line.explanation: White chases the knight, but moving the h-pawn creates the hook Black needs.
Black supports the knight and invites White to open the h-file.
White takes the bait and removes the pawn that was shielding the king.
Black's h-pawn recaptures and opens the rook's file toward the king.
White's knight tries to help defend h2, but it blocks an escape route.
The queen joins the open h-file and creates a direct mating threat.
White makes room, but the f-pawn move removes another square from the king.
Black's pawn reaches g3 and seals the king behind its own pieces.
The rook tries to block the second rank.
The knight joins with check threats and covers key escape squares.
The king steps toward f1, but the h-pawn continues forward.
Black removes the knight and creates a pawn one step from promotion.
The king tries to run toward the center.
The pawn promotes with check and forces White to block.
The bishop blocks the new queen's check.
The promoted queen removes the bishop with check.
White's king captures the promoted queen, but the original queen still controls the h-file.
Black's original queen returns to h1 and delivers checkmate.

ruy-lopez.success_message: Opening the h-file lets Black's rook, queen, and g-pawn build a mating net around the castled king.

philidor-defense.name: Philidor's Legal Mate
philidor-defense.danger: White's knight on e5 appears to expose the queen, but taking the queen allows Bxf7+ followed by Nd5 mate.
philidor-defense.how_to_avoid: Capture the knight on e5. Do not take the queen while White's bishop and knight can reach f7 and d5.

defense_line.explanation: The d6 pawn takes the knight and removes the piece needed for mate on d5.

philidor-defense.description: A version of Legal's Mate in the Philidor Defense.

trap_line.explanation: Attack the bishop.
The bishop retreats, maintaining the pin.
Sacrifice! Offering the queen.
Black takes the queen, but...
Check!
The only move.
Checkmate! Legal's Mate strikes again.

philidor-defense.success_message: Legal's Mate in the Philidor! A classic queen sacrifice.

philidor-defense.name: Damiano Defense Punishment
philidor-defense.danger: After Nxe5, recapturing with the f-pawn opens the queen's route to h5 and leaves Black's king unable to castle.
philidor-defense.how_to_avoid: Do not recapture the knight with ...fxe5. Play ...Qe7, attack the knight, and keep the f-pawn in front of the king.

defense_line.explanation: Black attacks the knight without opening the f-file or exposing the king to Qh5.

philidor-defense.description: Black plays 2...f6 (the Damiano), inviting a knight sacrifice that exposes the king to forced attack.

trap_line.explanation: Knight takes the pawn — looks risky but it's strong!
If Black takes, the king is exposed.
Check! The king cannot block with a piece.
Forced — Kg6 loses to Qf5+, and pawn moves don't defend.
White takes the second center pawn with check and keeps Black's king in the open.
Black's king moves again because it cannot block the queen's check.
White develops the bishop with check and brings another attacker into the game.
Black blocks the bishop's diagonal with the d-pawn.
The bishop removes the blocking pawn and checks again.
The king runs to g6, far from its starting shelter.
White takes away g5 and prepares to open more lines near the king.
Black stops h5 but leaves the queenside rook and pawns exposed.
White takes another pawn; the four captured pawns now outweigh the sacrificed knight.

philidor-defense.success_message: White uses repeated checks to recover four pawns for the knight while Black's king remains exposed.

philidor-defense.name: Philidor Legal's Mate
philidor-defense.description: Same pattern as Legal's Mate. White sacrifices the queen, then Bxf7+ Ke7 Nd5# is checkmate. Works when Black's bishop takes the queen greedily. Black should NOT take the queen. Play dxe5 to stay safe.

trap_line.explanation: White offers the queen by moving the pinned knight and aims both minor pieces at f7.
Black takes the queen and leaves the f7 square without enough defenders.
The bishop takes on f7 with check and pulls Black's king away from e8.
The king must step to e7, where the two white knights control its remaining flight squares.
The c3 knight lands on d5 with check. The bishop covers e8 and the e5 knight covers f7 and f3, leaving no legal escape.

philidor-defense.danger: Taking White's queen after Nxe5 allows Bxf7+ followed by Nd5 mate.
philidor-defense.how_to_avoid: Ignore the queen and remove the knight on e5 with the d6 pawn.

defense_line.explanation: The d6 pawn captures the knight. Black removes a mating attacker instead of grabbing the queen.

philidor-defense.success_message: Philidor Legal's Mate — the punishment lands. Same pattern as Legal's Mate. White sacrifices the queen, then Bxf7+ Ke7 Nd5# is...

petrov-defense.name: Stafford Gambit Trap
petrov-defense.danger: After Black's knight takes on e4, White's bishop on g5 is attacked and the queen-side back rank is vulnerable. Taking the queen on d8 allows a forced mate.
petrov-defense.how_to_avoid: Move the queen to e2 and keep defending f2 instead of taking Black's queen.

defense_line.explanation: The queen keeps f2 defended and steps away from the mating net. Material can wait until the king is safe.

petrov-defense.description: A dangerous gambit where Black sacrifices a pawn for a mating attack!

trap_line.explanation: White takes the knight.
Black recaptures.
White develops cautiously.
Black develops aggressively.
White pins the knight.
Black sacrifices!
White takes the queen, but...

french-defense.name: French Winawer Poisoned Pawn
french-defense.danger: White's queen attacks g7 and h7. Black should not make a slow move while those pawns and the king are exposed.
